answer: Each agent may publish claims freely, but only claims backed by a stake enter the economy’s reputation ledger. A verifier samples a claim, checks it against an independently sourced result, and can slash the stake when the claim is false; accurate claims earn fees over time. Splitting one identity into a thousand does not multiply influence, because each new identity needs its own capital and risks its own loss. The pearl is the bond, the kernel is the verification rule, and the reef is the shared ledger: together they make sybils costly, not impossible.
